messages:
maya: Reopening the convo on calibration signals for low-bit paths — noticed a few prod customers spiking in hallucination after FP8 rollouts. Need a defensible, low-overhead monitor + backstop plan.

drew: Yikes. Any quick indicators from the canary runs?

maya: Canary showed small but consistent top-1 token drift; distribution shift in head activations. I sliced by prompt length — long-context tails worse.

alan: Can we add a headwise loss delta metric? Compare float baseline vs low-bit shadow for the same tokens and aggregate across heads. Quick to compute if we sample kv-cache hits.

maya: Exactly what I had in mind. Headwise KL or signed loss-diff per-head -> aggregate percentile.

sophia: KL's nice but noisy on sparse tokens. Suggest median + 95th percentile, and a small exponential moving average to avoid flapping.

drew: Implementation questions: do we shadow-run full float on every request? Not feasible. We should sample epsilon fraction (0.1%) and only for sensitive endpoints.

maya: Agreed. Shadow-sampling + offline replay for richer evaluation. For online we keep headwise diffs and a compact histogram.

alan: Fallback policy: hysteresis required. If aggregate headwise delta > threshold for X minutes, revert to higher precision model for that endpoint. Also add per-customer override to skip low-bit.

sophia: +1. Also record tokenwise confidence and log examples for manual triage (link to S3 bucket).

ops-bot: Deploy notice: rolling canary for fp8-hotpath v2 scheduled 17:40 UTC.

drew: For thresholds, propose two bands: warn (soft) at median diff 0.02 + 95p 0.1, and hard at median 0.05 + 95p 0.25. Values are placeholders — we'll calibrate with replay.

maya: Sounds reasonable as a starting point. We should also monitor downstream metrics: rerank score variance and user-facing regression tests (sanity prompts).

alan: One more safety net: per-request quick micro-benchmark — if kv-cache hit rate drops or latency spikes when using low-bit path, prefer fallback.

sophia: Ops needs the signal shape for alerting. Maya, can you sketch the metric names and CCR thresholds?

maya: Will do. Proposed metrics: lowbit.head_diff.median, lowbit.head_diff.95p, lowbit.token_confidence.delta_median, lowbit.latency.delta; CCR: warn/hard as Drew suggested.

alan: For storage size, keep head diffs as compressed histograms (t-digest) + periodic flush. No per-token retention.

drew: API surface: expose per-endpoint quality_score and a boolean lowbit_allowed flag. Runtime can flip per-route.

sophia: Add audit logs for each automatic fallback event (reason, last values, actuation id). Compliance needs that.

maya: I'll open a follow-up RFC with: sampling plan, metric definitions, thresholds, fallback playbook, and operator runbook. Tagging eng-runtime and eng-platform for implementation work.

alan: Can we include a small shadow-eval harness that runs a fixed prompt set on both float and low-bit nightly and emits regression alerts?

maya: Yes — nightly replay + auto-bisect of model variant if regression crosses threshold.

ops-bot: Incident template: lowbit-quality-regression ready in /playbooks/quality.

sophia: Great. Who wants to own the RFC? Maya?

maya: I will. Draft by EOD tomorrow, include sample SQL for extracting head diffs and a small perf budget estimate.

drew: Happy to help with runtime hooks and throttling logic.

alan: I'll prototype the t-digest histogram exporter this week.

sophia: I'll coordinate alerts and compliance logging.

maya: Thanks all — this should give us fast detection + graceful fallback without huge cost. Will ping when RFC is up. :thumbsup:
